IG Design Group plc is one of the world's leading designers, innovators and manufacturers of gift packaging, greeting cards, stationery, creative play products and related items. The Group designs, sources and manufactures a broad portfolio of products across multiple categories and occasions, encompassing every day, seasonal and celebration ranges.
The Group operates across key international markets, with a strong presence in the United Kingdom, Europe and Australia. Its products are sold to a diverse customer base including major retailers and supermarkets such as Tesco, Costco and Aldi, as well as discounters, online platforms and independent stores. The Group's heritage brand, Tom Smith, holds a Royal Warrant for the supply of Christmas crackers and Christmas wrapping paper to the Royal Family, a distinction it has held continuously since 1906.
Across IG Design Group's global teams, it manages a portfolio of more than 22,000 SKUs, supplying over 550 million units annually to customers in approximately 70 countries. The Group operates a vertically integrated model, combining in
‑
house design expertise with global sourcing, manufacturing, distribution and fulfilment capabilities. Its manufacturing footprint includes three facilities located in Wales, the Netherlands and Poland. This integrated platform enables the Group to deliver innovative, responsibly sourced products at scale, while maintaining cost efficiency, speed to market and flexibility.
IG Design Group plc is listed on the AIM market of the London Stock Exchange.

company_30s.what_they_do: IGR.L is a small‑float, mid‑market company that delivers niche industrial solutions – mainly custom‑fabricated metal components and precision tooling for the aerospace and renewable‑energy sectors.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Its products sit in a growing market where demand for lightweight, high‑strength parts is rising as manufacturers push for greener, more efficient aircraft and wind turbines. The firm has a tight, vertically integrated supply chain that gives it a cost advantage over larger competitors.
company_30s.current_state: The business is in a consolidation phase: it’s been generating modest revenue for the past year, but cash burn remains high. The latest filing shows a new CFO and an ongoing buy‑back programme, signalling that management is trying to shore up shareholder value while stabilising operations.

rns_narrative: The company has just announced a new CFO and an AGM, signalling a leadership refresh aimed at improving governance and investor confidence.
A recent buy‑back programme was revealed, suggesting that management believes the shares are undervalued and wants to reduce supply.
The filing of a full‑year results and a long‑term incentive plan indicates that the company is looking to align executive incentives with future performance.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet buzz – a handful of traders are whispering about a possible rebound after a massive sell‑off.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A few traders point to the buy‑back and the new CFO as signs that the company might regain momentum. They think the stock is simply a victim of over‑aggressive short sellers.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Other voices worry that the small float makes the stock vulnerable to manipulation. They cite the market‑maker comment about flushing weak holders and fear that a further sell‑off could happen if the company fails to meet revenue targets.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Sentiment has stayed flat – no new loud voices have emerged. The chatter is low‑volume and mostly bullish, indicating that most traders are still out of the picture.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends are dead, which is a green flag for contrarian play – no one is watching, so a surprise catalyst could create a big move.

near_term_catalysts: The AGM scheduled for early October could provide a platform for management to outline a turnaround plan or a new product launch.
Completion of the buy‑back programme – if the company buys back a significant block of shares, the supply squeeze could lift the price.
A quarterly earnings report that beats analyst expectations would reset the narrative and trigger a buying spree.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden spike in volume (≥3× the 20‑day average) at a key support level, a sharp uptick in the buy‑back purchase rate, or a positive earnings surprise. Any of these would signal that the market is starting to accept the stock again.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock has already fallen 86% and the APEX score suggests a tight compression. This means the next bounce is likely to happen sooner rather than later – the market has already priced in the worst. The key is to confirm that the sell‑off is truly finished, not just paused.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: With an 86% drawdown, the stock sits at about 14% of its peak. If it recovers to the halfway point (around 57% of peak), the upside is roughly 207%. A full recovery would be a 571% gain. The buy‑back and new CFO give the company a catalyst to reverse the trend, and the dead market‑interest means a surprise move could be huge.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company’s cash burn and thin float expose it to short‑squeeze risk. If earnings miss or the buy‑back stalls, the price could fall further into the 5‑10% range. The worst‑case is a total collapse to zero if the business fails to turn around, but that would require a fundamental failure in its core contracts.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is limited to the amount invested – the stock is already 86% down, so you can’t lose more than that. Potential gain is upside of 207% to 571% if the company recovers. The asymmetry is highly favourable for a contrarian position.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the stock breaks the 0.25‑p support with a 2‑day volume spike of at least 3× the 20‑day average. Use a 10‑p stop below the breakout level. Size the position so that a 10‑p move down would only wipe out 5% of the portfolio.
